clue.text: Judge passing notice grabbed by one royal supporter

indicators.note: something grabbed by another is held inside it, so the notice goes within the one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice
an obit is an obituary, a notice of someone's passing

explanation.surface: A judge spots a death notice and some loyal monarchist snatches it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jacobites backed the exiled Stuart kings James II and his heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical term for an adherent of the deposed Stuart line, hence a partisan of a claimant to the throne.

clue.text: Parties starting with good French wine

indicators.note: the parties begin with the good letter, so it is placed at the front

parts.note: raves are big dance parties

explanation.surface: Celebrations that kick off with a decent bottle from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a Bordeaux region whose red and white wines carry its name.

clue.text: One who likes collecting international notes, principally?

definitions.text: One who likes collecting international notes, principally?

indicators.note: the liker collects, i.e. takes in, the next letters

parts.note: a fancier is someone keen on something, like a pigeon fancier

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of the word notes

explanation.surface: A hobbyist who gathers foreign banknotes, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a money man is chiefly fond of amassing banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A money specialist naturally relishes amassing cash, so the whole clue is a playful description of one.

clue.text: Stand right beside northern river

indicators.note: the right letter sits beside the river name, here after it

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone positioned on the bank of a river up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire flows through Leeds in Yorkshire. 'Stand' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes-drying frame is a kind of stand on which washing is hung.

clue.text: Finally recognised compere of University Challenge

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: At last somebody identified the quizmaster of the TV show University Challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: University Challenge is a long-running British TV quiz; the show's name is split so 'Challenge' becomes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge an order or opponent is to resist or dare it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Match official leads the French team on, it's thought

indicators.note: the official leads, coming first in front of the rest

parts.note: a ref is a referee
le is French for the
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
taken as written

explanation.surface: A referee heads out in front of a French side.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an older spelling of reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflection is a considered idea or meditation, so it is a thought.

clue.text: Place of research using the speeches of Ramsay MacDonald?

parts.note: Ramsay MacDonald was the first Labour prime minister, and Lab is short for Labour
oratory is the art or body of public speaking

explanation.surface: A historian studies the first Labour premier's speeches in some research setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramsay MacDonald led Britain's first Labour government in 1924.
explanation.definitionFit: A lab is a room equipped for scientific experiment and study.

clue.text: Boss, outspoken person of high position

indicators.note: outspoken signals that the word is said aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a nob is a toff or person of high social rank

explanation.surface: A boss is a blunt, outspoken big shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' means a raised stud, not a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round raised projection, like the stud on a shield, which is a rounded lump.

clue.text: Type of accommodation — you rent middle parts out

indicators.note: the middle letters of each word are taken out: the O of you and the EN of rent

explanation.surface: An advert for lodging that says you let out the central rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mongolian circular felt tent is a kind of dwelling, so a type of lodging.

clue.text: Scruffy kid beginning to read afresh, having admitted mistake

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of read
the word for afresh lets the mistake in, holding it inside

parts.note: afresh means again
a muff is a blunder, as in muffing a catch

explanation.surface: A messy child starting to read once more after making an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragged, dirty urchin is a scruffy youngster, so the two terms match.

clue.text: Forest dweller cross about rubbish container in front of house

indicators.note: the cross goes around the next pieces

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix or cross, as in rood screen

indicators.note: the container comes before the house letter

parts.note: a bin holds rubbish

explanation.surface: A woodland resident, annoyed about a bin outside the front of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry, but it is the rood.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw lived in Sherwood Forest, so he is literally a forest dweller.

clue.text: Conducted in lively manner? Not this French oral exam

indicators.note: not means the following part is left out

parts.note: vivace is the musical direction to play in a lively way
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A spoken test in French, run briskly, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral exam' is short for viva voce, the spoken defence of a thesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is a spoken examination, typically defending a dissertation before examiners.

clue.text: Shelter by side of a large pathway

indicators.note: the shelter is set beside the other letters, here after them

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A refuge next to a big walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: An allée is a formal tree-lined walk in a garden or park, so a kind of path.

clue.text: Critical about national party's split

indicators.note: the critical word goes around the party

parts.note: severe can mean critical, as with a serious illness
the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: A serious row over a nationalist party leading to a breakaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party's' reads as party is, the 's being the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Severance is the act of cutting apart, a division or separation.

clue.text: Obligation hospital accepted to provide health drink

indicators.note: the obligation accepts, taking in, the hospital

parts.note: a tie is a binding obligation
san is short for sanatorium, a type of hospital

explanation.surface: A duty accepted by a hospital to supply a healthy beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion is drunk for its supposed medicinal benefits.

clue.text: Heroine in novel is ensnared by devious rascal

indicators.note: is gets caught inside the scrambled letters
devious suggests something twisted out of its straight form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A storybook heroine is trapped by a scheming scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' gives CLARSA, and 'ensnared by' sets the second word of the clue inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Richardson's eighteenth-century novel is named after its title heroine, pursued by the rake Lovelace.

clue.text: Second of Fijian houses overthrown

indicators.note: in a down clue, overthrown means turned upside down, so reversed
houses means contains, so the letters sit within of Fijian

explanation.surface: Second among Fijian homes toppled, maybe by a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal, but it means a moment. 'overthrown' turns FFIJ, taken from 'of Fijian', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a very short moment, as in back in a jiffy.

clue.text: Rush to cover up clangers and bloomers

parts.note: a canter is a brisk pace, a rush along
to bury something is to cover it up
bells clang

explanation.surface: Hurrying to hide embarrassing mistakes and blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clangers' and 'bloomers' are British slang for gaffes, but here they are bells and flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are flowering plants, a campanula with bell-shaped blooms, so they are bloomers.

clue.text: Abandoned body near cemetery

indicators.note: abandoned implies thrown about without restraint, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A corpse dumped beside a graveyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a graveyard, a place where bones lie buried.

clue.text: German city, one hears

definitions.meaning: An ancient city on the Moselle in Germany
someone who hears a case in court, judging it

explanation.surface: A German city, so I'm told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' seems to flag a sound-alike, but it is a second definition: one who tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or juror who tries a case hears it; the city is the Moselle town, Germany's oldest.

clue.text: Meandered in capital city, round area close to fairground

indicators.note: the city goes round the other letters

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of fairground

explanation.surface: Someone strolled in a capital, around a district near a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander aimlessly is to meander, a synonym for drifting about.

clue.text: Steven's interpretation?

parts.note: the name Steven's is a rearrangement, a version, of the word events

explanation.surface: How one man called Steven reads things.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase works backwards: a 'version' of EVENTS, rearranged, gives STEVENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's account of what happened is their interpretation of it.

clue.text: Musicians in series not allowed on the radio

parts.note: a string is a series, as in a string of wins

indicators.note: on the radio means it is heard, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: banned means not allowed

explanation.surface: Players in a programme run that the broadcasters have forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of players on violins, cellos and so on is an ensemble of musicians.

clue.text: Leading academic or postgraduate producing document

parts.note: a prof, professor, is a senior academic
taken as written
an MA is a Master of Arts, a postgraduate

explanation.surface: A senior professor or graduate student generating paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: A pro forma is a standard form or invoice issued in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a template form or provisional invoice, a type of paper.

clue.text: Be out of form, naturally struggling to shed pounds during training

indicators.note: the remaining letters go inside the training letters

parts.note: PT is physical training

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
to shed means one of the jumbled letters is dropped

parts.note: L stands for pounds, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: An athlete off form, of course, battling to lose weight during workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is a British school class, not fitness. 'struggling' and 'to shed' leave the jumble LAYTRUAN, which 'during' places inside the training letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip school is to be absent from one's class, which a form is in British schools.

clue.text: Kid is about forty-five minutes, possibly, in Chinese restaurant

indicators.note: the kidding word goes around the time

parts.note: to kid is to tease
three quarters of an hour, so three quarters of the four letters of hour

explanation.surface: Someone joking about a three-quarter-hour wait at a Chinese eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is a verb. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese or Japanese establishment serving tea and refreshments, so a kind of eatery.

clue.text: One trembles, note, when brought before monarch

indicators.note: the note is placed before the monarch

parts.note: a quaver is a musical note, an eighth note
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone shaking when hauled before the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose voice wobbles or shakes is a trembler; 'one trembles' describes such a person.

clue.text: A new cleric from S American region

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A newly appointed clergyman from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things from the Andes mountain range of South America.

clue.text: Put spicy coating on trimmed meat daughter served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are read upwards, so reversed
trimmed means the end letter is cut off

parts.note: liver is offal, eaten as meat

explanation.surface: A cook seasoning a cut of meat before serving it to a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' turns LIVER into LIVE; with D it is LIVED, which 'served up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To devil food is to cook it with hot spices like mustard or cayenne, as in devilled kidneys.

clue.text: Regularly feed team cheese

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An instruction to give the side some cheese at fixed intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek brined curd made from sheep's or goat's milk is a well-known cheese.
